author: OpenAI Codex assessment agent (thinker_assessments, contemporary follow-up)
changeNote: First complete 240-question assessment under the current 15 Values bank and scoring. Documented positions, user-authorised sound inferences and supported conditional neutral answers are distinguished. An independent evidence audit amended interpretation and source errors before archiving; substantive findings are recorded in review.notes. No 12Axes questions or scores were imported.

metadata.name: Julia Gillard
metadata.description: Australian Labor prime minister whose minority government enacted carbon pricing and disability and school reforms, while retaining offshore asylum processing and opposing same-sex marriage during her premiership.
metadata.scope: Personal positions and governing conduct during 2010–2013. Coalition measures are attributed cautiously. Modern hypothetical policies are labelled inferred, not claimed as direct statements. Research cutoff 4 October 2026; later views do not overwrite a former governing period.

sources.title: Press conference: regional processing and humanitarian places

Gillard will not pretend religion for votes
Social Security Legislation Amendment (Fair Incentives to Work) Act 2012: human-rights scrutiny
Clean Energy (Household Assistance Amendments) Bill 2011: enacted household cash assistance
New York press conference: Libya no-fly zone and carbon-pricing household assistance

axes.brief: Parliamentary democracy and negotiated minority government structure political authority.
axes.counterEvidence: Party-room leadership replacement is constitutionally parliamentary and should not be confused with abolishing public elections.

answers.rationale: Her minority government depended on an election and continuing parliamentary confidence.
Expert reviews informed policy without replacing elected government.
Her civic account celebrates equal participation rather than educational voting qualifications.
Minority-government bargaining treated parliamentary support as necessary for legislation.
Opposition competition remained legitimate despite bitter political confrontation.
Minority parliamentary scrutiny was integral to her government's operation.
The Malaysia-plan judgment constrained her policy; she sought legislative change rather than denying courts' authority.
Labor's union links did not substitute union appointment for public elections.
Her democratic practice allowed opponents to campaign freely.
Constitutional referendums are legitimate, while ordinary legislation remains primarily parliamentary.
Negotiated coalition support contradicts unilateral prime-ministerial legislative authority.
Losing parliamentary-party support ended her premiership through constitutional mechanisms.
She announced an election date rather than claiming indefinite personal authority.
Electoral accountability matters, but representative terms and parliamentary removal supply alternatives to automatic recall.
Her government depended on continuing confidence and public electoral accountability.
Her defence policy retained civilian control rather than military political supremacy.

axes.brief: Civil liberties coexist with preventive policing, public-health regulation and security restrictions.
axes.counterEvidence: Offshore detention and tobacco regulation qualify a strongly libertarian reading.

answers.rationale: Public-health regulation and retained drug prohibition qualify individual choice over risky substances.
Court-authorised investigation fits her lawful policing and national-security approach.
Peaceful assembly is legitimate, while proportionate restrictions can protect transport and public order.
Her rejection of extremist intimidation supports lawful criticism, though speech protections coexist with antidiscrimination law.
Tobacco regulation shows willingness to constrain personal consumption for public health.
Security prevention matters, but indefinite universal tracking goes beyond ordinary targeted enforcement.
Preventing impaired driving fits her acceptance of proportionate public-safety intervention.
Independent judicial findings make preventative restrictions more consistent with her institutional approach.
Plural expression deserves protection, while her antidiscrimination framework permits some limits on seriously harmful expression.
Political anonymity deserves protection, but investigation and accountability can justify identification in defined cases.
Immediate danger may justify limited searches, while equal treatment and legal safeguards constrain suspicionless powers.
Her response to violent disorder supports proportionate restrictions on gatherings with credible serious risks.
Judicial authorization is the normal safeguard, with genuinely urgent safety exceptions.
Public-interest disclosure supports accountability, while national-security confidentiality remains a competing duty.
Australia’s restrictive licensing model does not accept personal defence as a routine justification for firearm ownership; Gillard retained that framework.
Her constitutional practice favours independent legal oversight even when counterterrorism restrictions are justified.

axes.brief: Official multiculturalism combines retained heritage with English learning and common civic responsibilities.
axes.counterEvidence: Her condemnation of extremism and emphasis on shared duties limit an interpretation of multiculturalism as civic separation.

answers.rationale: Her multiculturalism treats minority traditions as contributors rather than automatically subordinate customs.
Access-and-equity commitments explicitly support adapting services to cultural diversity.
Common civic responsibilities and English learning matter without requiring wholesale cultural replacement.
Her multicultural policy expressly permits maintaining diverse cultural backgrounds.
English learning is presented as an important route to civic participation.
Indigenous recognition and inclusive citizenship support visible acknowledgment in national occasions.
Shared traditions can receive support, but multicultural access resists exclusive funding preference.
Her multiculturalism stresses common civic responsibilities rather than separate identities overriding shared citizenship.
Shared holidays aid cohesion while plural observance warrants accommodation.
Multiple cultural backgrounds form part of her account of Australian nationhood.
Her speeches distinguish inclusive participation from divisive separation.

Her access-and-equity multiculturalism supports community languages on public signs alongside broadly accessible English. This inference concerns public information, not simply private commercial expression.
Her policy permits family heritage to coexist with national civic membership.
Reasonable religious accommodation follows equal access, constrained by concrete identification needs.
She explicitly describes multiculturalism as central to Australia's national identity.
Civic integration in her account is compatible with maintaining community cultures.

axes.brief: Managed skilled and family migration coexist with expanded humanitarian places and offshore deterrence.
axes.counterEvidence: Offshore processing was restored during Gillard; the later Rudd government's permanent PNG exclusion policy must not be misattributed to her.

answers.rationale: Her controlled migration programme weighs population capacity and labour-market needs.
Migration is nation-building, but improved living conditions alone do not override regulated eligibility.
Skilled migration is important, while family and humanitarian pathways remain legitimate.
Family reunion fits her inclusive migration system, subject to eligibility and programme constraints.
Expanded humanitarian places support protection not determined by cultural similarity or economic utility.
Offshore processing and deterrence weigh against routine permission to remain after irregular entry.
Employment demand does not eliminate capacity, labour standards or admission controls.
Service capacity matters, while her nation-building account recognises migrants' substantial contributions.
Family places remain part of a managed programme rather than automatically outside numerical planning.
Work opportunities support eligibility but do not make a job offer sufficient on its own.

Employer and family sponsorship are important channels, while independently assessed skilled and humanitarian applicants qualify through different routes. Family reunion is itself one of the sponsors named in the question.
Education exports and student mobility do not imply automatic permanent residence for every graduate.
She expanded humanitarian numbers, but retained designated routes and managed resettlement rather than unconditional cap exemptions.
Multicultural citizenship rejects cultural resemblance as a general refugee-selection principle.
Basic protection and lawful status matter, while benefit entitlements can vary by residency and visa conditions.
Cultural diversity enriches nation-building, but admissions also serve family, humanitarian and economic purposes.

axes.brief: US alliance and sustained deployments combine with regional diplomacy and multilateral engagement.
axes.counterEvidence: Professional forces and diplomacy qualify militarism; alliance commitments do not establish support for every speculative weapons technology.

answers.rationale: Afghanistan and alliance commitments permit force beyond direct territorial defence.
Regional diplomacy and multilateral cooperation receive priority where viable.
Maintaining credible alliance capabilities warrants substantial spending, tempered by fiscal constraints.
Imminent threats can justify preventive defence, but alliance loyalty alone does not warrant unconstrained pre-emption.

Afghanistan can be understood as a response to an attack on an ally, so that deployment alone does not refute the statement. Her support for UN consideration of a Libya no-fly zone favours humanitarian force in principle, while not directly committing Australian forces; this leaves a mixed inference on the rule governing her own country.
Her military policy relies on professional forces rather than universal male service.
Negotiation can avoid war, while alliance commitments limit concessions that undermine security.
A hypothetical autonomous killing system raises accountability risks beyond her support for conventional defence technology.
Continued overseas commitments require more than invasion-repelling capability.
Her alliance policy rejects peace at any cost to partners.
Continued Afghan involvement demonstrates acceptance of sustained foreign deployments.
Peaceful regional dispute resolution is generally preferable to escalating unresolved territorial claims.
Deterrence assists diplomacy, but coercive threats are not her universal negotiating preference.
Avoiding conflict matters alongside credible allied commitments and defence obligations.
National-security cooperation accepts intelligence gathering despite possible diplomatic tension.
Verified reciprocal reductions can support her cooperative security approach without disarming unilaterally.

axes.brief: International cooperation is accepted within continuing Australian constitutional sovereignty.
axes.counterEvidence: Border control and domestic constitutional authority constrain unrestricted supranational decision-making.

answers.rationale: Australian constitutional authority remains central despite international commitments.
Multilateral agreements can bind Australia, but domestic democratic approval and core autonomy retain weight.
Domestic constitutional interpretation remains for Australian courts.
Her close US alliance accepts enduring strategic obligations.
International commitments are voluntary political choices, though withdrawal has diplomatic and legal costs.
Rule-based international accountability fits her multilateral orientation, subject to agreed jurisdiction.
National interests and shared international solutions are treated as mutually important rather than categorically ranked.

Climate cooperation and domestic carbon pricing support shared action, but neither alone transfers environmental decisions to an international institution. Her national instruments and regional cooperation support a conditional balance.

Regional cooperation and the US alliance preserve substantial independent Australian diplomacy. Participation alone does not show support for joining a bloc that requires a common foreign policy; willingness to cooperate is balanced against national discretion.
Rights oversight is legitimate, but unrestricted external authority to rewrite domestic law goes beyond her constitutional practice.
Her economic programme retains Australia's independent currency.
Regional and international programmes can legitimately share funding and decisions.
Strong migration controls preserve national admission authority despite regional processing cooperation.
Her trade and regional economic engagement accept common rules.
Her internationalism does not seek Australia's absorption into a larger federation.
Credible agreements entail accepting some near-term domestic costs for sustained cooperation.

axes.brief: Mixed ownership includes private enterprise, public services and strategic broadband infrastructure.
axes.counterEvidence: Public broadband is a specific strategic intervention, not an economy-wide nationalisation programme.

answers.rationale: Her government maintains a mixed economy dominated by private firms.
Essential networks can warrant public ownership, illustrated by the public broadband rollout.
Public and private delivery can both be legitimate; demonstrable public accountability matters beyond nominal performance equivalence.
NBN construction shows willingness to establish a public enterprise where market provision is inadequate.
Medicare and public hospitals support a substantial public-provider role alongside private medicine.
Shared rail infrastructure can justify continuing public ownership and investment.
Cost savings matter, but labour standards and long-term accountability qualify automatic outsourcing.
Public development finance may fill gaps, while her programme does not imply a general public retail-banking system.
Ordinary holdings can be sold, but retained public strategic purpose matters more than sale proceeds alone.
Social housing fits her concern with secure access alongside private housing provision.
Regulated private ownership remains legitimate where strategic goals are genuinely protected.
Resource-rent taxation seeks a public share of private extraction returns rather than general nationalisation.
Contracting can work when quality and workforce protections are real, without being an unconditional default.
NBN policy values strategic public control rather than merely immediate privatisation receipts.
Commercial losses warrant reform, while essential access can justify continued public support.
Public broadcasters support national and multicultural communication consistent with her public-service approach.

axes.brief: Regional trade openness coexists with selective industry support and national-interest screening.
axes.counterEvidence: Industry assistance qualifies free trade but does not imply broad permanent import substitution.

answers.rationale: Regional economic engagement favours open trade, with selective domestic industry support.
Competition and regional market access can outweigh losses for some incumbent firms.
Local employment objectives compete with cost-effective procurement and international commitments.
Export-oriented firms benefit from competitive imported inputs in her open-economy framework.
Essential resilience can justify exceptions, but routine restriction of cheaper imports is not her general method.
Her engagement emphasises negotiated liberalisation more clearly than universal unilateral tariff elimination.

Industry assistance can help emerging sectors, but subsidies and investment do not themselves restrict imports. Her open-trade commitments balance targeted domestic support; neither blanket opposition nor a general temporary infant-industry tariff rule follows.
Foreign investment is welcome subject to national-interest review.
Agricultural export interests favour openness, while adjustment and domestic safeguards remain relevant.
Education and skills are preferred adjustment tools within a trading economy.
Fair access matters, but multilateral dispute resolution can be preferable to escalating reciprocal tariffs.
Nondiscriminatory market rules fit her regional trading approach.
Demonstrable subsidised competition can justify targeted trade remedies.
Regional agreements can lower barriers despite increasing economic interdependence.
Strategic investment review can block particular takeovers without rejecting foreign capital generally.
Education and digital service exports favour cross-border access within domestic regulatory safeguards.

axes.brief: Market production is supplemented by industrial investment, wage regulation and national service planning.
axes.counterEvidence: A national school plan is not a compulsory economy-wide production plan.

answers.rationale: Private firms ordinarily retain decisions about what to produce.
National education goals are not compulsory business production quotas.
Market prices ordinarily allocate goods, with intervention for defined public purposes.
Broadband, education and clean-energy investment demonstrate deliberate sector priorities.
Entry and exit generally respond to demand within employment and regulatory protections.
Affordability can warrant essential-service controls, but broad price administration is not her economic default.
Business formation is generally permitted without proving official production need.
Public investment can influence credit priorities while ordinary bank lending remains private.
Open capital movement is compatible with her economy, constrained by security and financial regulation.
Industry and clean-energy assistance permit targeted subsidies.

Private financial innovation can fit her mixed economy, while monetary stability and consumer protection justify regulation. Competition with official currency does not require replacing it or permitting unrestricted issuance; the resulting inference is conditional.
Her labour-market approach supports enforceable minimum wages.
Collective bargaining and legal floors coexist with negotiated wages rather than general official wage schedules.
Central-bank autonomy is more consistent with her framework than a binding national output plan.
Rental affordability can justify intervention, but private rents remain broadly market-based alongside assistance.
Strategic public investment does not imply routinely planning all production and distribution.

axes.brief: Needs-based education and disability inclusion justify progressive financing, tempered by work incentives and fiscal discipline.
axes.counterEvidence: Changes to parenting payments and budget discipline constrain an unqualified expansionary-welfare interpretation.

answers.rationale: Needs-based services and progressive financing seek to reduce material disadvantage.
Unequal opportunity supplies a legitimate redistribution rationale beyond absolute destitution.

Higher disability and school spending expanded services, but the transfer of some single parents to lower Newstart payments restrained their cash-income floor. Targeted family assistance and cash-benefit restraint support a mixed judgment on a stronger minimum income financed by higher taxes.

Family payments and clean-energy cash supplements extend assistance beyond survival, while the move of some parents to lower Newstart payments shows limits on narrowing living-standard differences. Disability and school services alone would not establish the cash-benefit proposition.
Progressive contributions and resource-rent taxation assign greater burdens where capacity is greater.
Work and enterprise deserve reward while taxation funds shared opportunity.
Her equity agenda recognises inherited advantage, but inheritance taxation was not a central governing instrument.

Moving eligible parents from Parenting Payment to Newstart reduced payments but retained a means-tested income-support route. It was not an automatic end to all income support after a fixed duration; job-search conditions are a separate mechanism.
Public contributions from wealth-related returns can be justified, but an annual general wealth levy is not her main instrument.

Her government expanded some family cash payments while reducing support for some single parents and pursuing fiscal restraint. These competing cash policies support a mixed assessment; NDIS and school spending alone do not answer how modest income benefits should be.

Her inclusion agenda values social participation, yet moving some parents to lower Newstart payments conflicts with a uniformly generous cash standard. NDIS service provision is relevant context but is not itself a cash income benefit.

The clean-energy compensation package combined income-tax cuts with cash supplements, while other benefit restraint supported fiscal objectives. Her governing record balances tax relief and payments rather than consistently putting one ahead of the other.
Support for working households and the tax-free threshold fits supplementing low earnings.
Her progressive tax framework rejects one marginal rate for all taxpayers.
Equal opportunity supports improving access, but compulsory broad land redistribution is not a natural extension of her programme.

Family Tax Benefit and clean-energy supplements extended cash support to eligible working families rather than restricting every payment to households unable to survive. These actual cash programmes support broad eligibility; NDIS and schooling services are distinct.

axes.brief: Civil authority and religious equality coexist with public support for faith-based services.
axes.counterEvidence: Personal atheism alone is not evidence for abolishing religious holidays, faith schools or every civic religious reference.

answers.rationale: Her personal nonbelief is distinct from policy; public reasons and equal citizenship support civil legislative justification.
Respect for faith does not make religious doctrine her general legislative source.
Her parliamentary system assigns no required clerical approval to laws.
Equal religious citizenship weighs against a constitution privileging one official faith.
Knowledge about different religions can serve inclusive education without promoting belief.
Public education should not compel adherence to a selected faith, despite continued faith-school support.
Civil legal authority does not depend on religious leadership.
Her parliamentary decision-making gives religious groups ordinary consultation rights, not an official review role attached to clerical authority.
Public ceremonies can include faith traditions without requiring every participant to worship.
Faith-based schools and services receive support, but promoting belief as such requires a separate justification.
Familiar religious symbolism can coexist with plural citizenship if it does not establish exclusive membership.

Retaining Christmas and Easter holidays supports continuity, while her pluralist civic account resists religious preference. Their practical observance does not by itself establish support for official recognition of the predominant faith.
Her constitutional practice does not reserve parliamentary seats for clergy.
Charitable treatment can include religion, but nonbelief and equal citizenship weaken exclusive faith-only fiscal privilege.
Civil marriage remains possible independently of religious officiants, even under her restrictive definition of marriage.
Civil family law and equal legal process take precedence over binding clerical courts.

axes.brief: Gender reform is substantial, but personal opposition to same-sex marriage limits the progressive assessment for this period.
axes.counterEvidence: Her later support for marriage equality is outside the 2010–2013 governing scope and does not replace her recorded 2012 vote.

answers.rationale: Gender equality and institutional reform support revising inherited customs when they exclude participation.
Her marriage position preserves one tradition while her gender programme challenges others.
She recognises varied households but withheld equal marriage status from same-sex couples while in office.
Her gender-equality advocacy rejects fixed adult roles based on sex.
Her 2012 parliamentary vote opposed legal same-sex marriage; later changes do not overwrite this period.
Stable families matter, but her own public position and equality agenda resist making one household form universally compulsory.
Her broader reproductive-rights and women's-autonomy orientation supports early abortion access, with medical safeguards.
Parental involvement is valuable while a national educational role protects access to basic health knowledge.
Opposition to same-sex marriage does not prove opposition to all same-sex parenting; child welfare and family equality pull differently.
Her gender-equality stance leaves adult dress largely a personal matter.
Respectful inclusive language fits equal participation, with legal compulsion a separate question.
Tradition informed her marriage view, but was not a universal priority over contemporary equality claims.
Her public challenge to sexism supports equal ambitions beyond conventional sex roles.
Her reform programme accepts major changes, while parliamentary compromise and community acceptance affect timing.
Inclusive education has value, but parental involvement and age-appropriate teaching remain legitimate considerations.
Heritage can have communal meaning without requiring preservation of every obsolete practice.

axes.brief: Education, broadband and innovation are promoted alongside health and environmental precautions.
axes.counterEvidence: Neural implants, advanced AI and embryo enhancement are explicitly inferred applications rather than historical personal statements.

answers.rationale: Broadband and research investment favour new technology where anticipated benefits are substantial.
Trials should resolve serious risks, while excessive delay can deny educational and economic benefits.
Infrastructure matters alongside carbon and environmental safeguards, requiring case-specific balancing.
Health protection supports substantial safety evidence before broad medicine release, allowing exceptions for urgent need.
Her skills-centred growth approach would favour productivity technology paired with worker training.
Environmental protection carries weight but does not automatically override all public infrastructure benefits.

Agricultural innovation can improve productivity and reduce some environmental pressures, while uncertain ecological effects warrant proportionate assessment. Environmental benefit and ecological risk, rather than consumer health alone, are the relevant competing considerations.
Invasive healthy-person implants require stronger long-term evidence than ordinary digital infrastructure.
Her carbon price combines technological incentives with changed consumption, rather than relying only on speculative breakthroughs.
Environmental assessment should address potentially serious irreversible impacts before construction proceeds.
Personal consent matters, but minimal initial safety alone is insufficient for an invasive neural device.
Medical diagnostic systems should be validated for reliability and equal treatment before general use.
Education-led opportunity reform supplies no clear reason to accept irreversible heritable enhancement risks in children.
Agricultural productivity and ecosystem protection justify proportionate evidence rather than categorical approval or indefinite prohibition.
Housing and transport can justify development, while significant habitat harms require mitigation or alternatives.
Serious irreversible harm warrants a higher evidence threshold despite support for technological progress.

axes.brief: Federal reform uses national standards and financing while retaining constitutionally significant states.
axes.counterEvidence: Intergovernmental agreements preserved implementation flexibility; national standards did not eliminate state powers.

answers.rationale: States retain constitutional powers even when national reform negotiations are difficult.
Federal powers and state jurisdiction both have constitutional standing.
Her federal constitutional practice does not recognise unilateral regional secession by simple local majority.
National equity goals can justify overriding obstructive rules within legitimate Commonwealth powers.
Regional constitutional arrangements are compatible with federation subject to national rights and law.
Ordinary policing remains substantially state-based rather than a single centrally controlled force.
Equalisation and nationally financed services weigh against regions keeping most revenue regardless of need elsewhere.
National curriculum and school-improvement standards express strong national coordination.
State and local fiscal choices are legitimate within constitutional and intergovernmental constraints.
National workplace protections supply common employment floors.
Local institutional adjustment should normally occur without routine Commonwealth permission, subject to state law.
National disability and health guarantees support common minimum treatment entitlements.
Indigenous recognition deserves institutional expression, while national service duties and rights constrain complete autonomy.
Fiscal coordination can limit harmful competition undermining national public-service funding.
Local knowledge matters, while environmental spillovers and national protections can justify higher-level decisions.
Cross-state disasters require coordinated national resources and response.

axes.brief: Educational and social opportunity receive substantial causal weight; biology remains relevant without supporting racial determinism.
axes.counterEvidence: Normative equal rights do not prove universal social causation. Mixed stress, empathy, temperament and physical-attractiveness preference answers preserve that distinction.

answers.rationale: Needs-based school funding assumes upbringing and learning opportunities substantially shape later capacities.

Her school-equity programme emphasises learning conditions and opportunity as explanations of achievement differences. This supports a modest inference against inherited national intelligence as the main account; rejecting discriminatory policy is not itself causal proof.
Her challenge to sexism assigns major causal weight to social expectations and unequal treatment.
Stress physiology and difficult social circumstances can interact; her disability and education policies recognise both kinds of influence.
Her educational programme explicitly seeks to change interests, skills and prospects through better experience.
Disposition can affect risk-taking, while opportunity and learning also alter it; neither is universally decisive.
Multicultural civic learning assumes cooperation can grow through contact and shared institutions.
Empathy includes individual disposition and learned perspective; inclusive education strengthens the latter without disproving the former.
Targeted learning support assumes attention and achievement respond to classroom and developmental conditions.
Moral traditions are learned, while individual emotional dispositions also matter; no universal biological priority follows.
Her multicultural contact programme assumes experience can reduce socially learned fear and hostility.
Disability policy recognises biological differences while education policy recognises development; temperament need not be exclusively either.

Her gender-equality and multicultural approach allows learned beauty standards to vary across communities, while physical attraction can also involve inherited dispositions; neither establishes universal predominance.

Multicultural participation and opportunity policies favour social explanations of racial crime disparities. The inference is qualified because civic equality does not establish the exact relative causal contributions.

Targeted education assumes that experience can improve self-regulation. This supports learned influences without claiming that her programme directly establishes the causes of every observed group difference.
Her gender-equality advocacy treats expectations and unequal opportunity as consequential to pay differences, alongside choices.

review.notes: Independently reviewed all 240 exact questions for the 2010–2013 period. Corrected cash-benefit claims that relied on NDIS and schooling services, and distinguished Parenting Payment transfer to Newstart from a complete time-limit cutoff. Balanced social-participation rhetoric against reduced parental cash benefits. Corrected public signage, employer-or-family sponsorship, international environmental authority versus cooperation, and compulsory common foreign policy versus alliance membership. Repaired the environmental substitution rationale and moderated causal claims that equality policy cannot prove. Retained her in-office opposition to same-sex marriage despite later changes, and did not infer clerical rule from public religious accommodation. Neutral answers identify actual competing considerations; technology and human-trait analogies remain interpretive. No similarity tuning; image validation and batch similarity are separate. Follow-up specificity check distinguished customary holidays from official religious recognition, and monetary or financial regulation from the exact private-currency and national-security ownership propositions where relevant. Independent close-neighbour review on 2026-10-04 compared exact answers, periods and policy mechanisms with anthony-albanese revision 1. Specific corrections and retention reasons are recorded in review.similarity; no score tuning was used. The close-pair source check also corrected military05: Afghanistan is not by itself proof of force outside responses to attacks on allies; Libya humanitarian-force support is weighed against no direct Australian combat commitment. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.

similarity.reason: Retain both revision 1 profiles after independent exact-question comparison. Gillard is confined to 2010–2013 minority-government conduct; Albanese is assessed through 4 October 2026, with current policies weighted. Both retain Labor mixed-economy, welfare, federal and alliance commitments, so close aggregate scores are expected. Their records sharply diverge on the exact marriage question (Gillard’s in-office opposition versus Albanese’s support). Gillard transferred some single parents to lower Newstart payments; Albanese expanded parenting eligibility and increased JobSeeker and rent assistance. Her carbon-price mechanism and national school agenda differ from his current industrial-investment, faster housing-development and migration-reduction priorities. Relevant item distinctions include progressive05, redistribution03/11, planning04/10, immigration08 and innovation15. Pair review corrected residual cash-versus-services rationales, subsidies-versus-import-restrictions, and constitutional-referendum-versus-ordinary-law-repeal reasoning, even though these corrections may increase aggregate resemblance. Distinct periods, policy mechanisms and opposite marriage positions warrant retaining both; scores were not tuned to clear the warning.
